papers.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
papers.abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.

papers.title: A frame-indifferent rank-one convex function in three dimensions which is not quasiconvex
papers.abstract: We construct a function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}\to\mathbb{R}$ which is frame-indifferent, $W(QF)=W(F)$ for all $Q\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$, rank-one convex, but not quasiconvex. In a neighbourhood of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ the function is an explicit polynomial of degree four in the strain $F^TF-\mathrm{Id}$; the failure of quasiconvexity occurs at $F=\mathrm{Id}$ through a third-order mechanism of \v{S}ver\'ak type, with test functions whose gradients are arbitrarily close to $\mathrm{Id}$. The polynomial is obtained from a geometrically linear example, a rank-one convex, non-quasiconvex quartic polynomial of the symmetric part of the gradient, by evaluating it at the strain $\frac12(F^TF-\mathrm{Id})$, adding a uniaxial prestress and a cubic correction, and enlarging the quartic term. The local function is extended to all of $\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}$ by adding a frame-indifferent polyconvex function which vanishes near $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. This work was carried out with the assistance of the AI model Claude Opus 5.5; the proofs of the main results have been formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Global regularity for 3D large spherically symmetric degenerate compressible Navier-Stokes equations with superlinear BD viscosity and far-field vacuum
papers.abstract: Superlinear density-dependent viscosity presents a fundamental obstacle of global regularity to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the presence of far-field vacuum: the viscous diffusion vanishes at infinity, so excluding vacuum on bounded sets does not suffice to control the flow globally. For $\alpha\in (1,11.7)$ and $\gamma\in [2\alpha-1,3\alpha-1)$ , we establish global regularity for arbitrarily large, strong, finite-mass initial data with positive density at every finite point and vacuum at infinity. First, we introduce new rescalsed variables regarding the velocity, effective velocity and mass, then we exploit several novel quantities near the center and employ a refined maximum principle to establish the Lipschitz continuity of the velocity at the center-thereby resolving the singularity of the velocity gradient. Another key mechanism is a quantitative control of material volume distortion that remains effective in the vacuum tail. Conservative estimates for the physical and effective velocity gradients yield uniformly vanishing exterior variation tails. These estimates identify a material trajectory with small cumulative Jacobian variation and lead to two-sided bounds for the exterior volume Jacobian, making the evolving density comparable to its initial value along particle paths. On spatial scales determined by the initial density, the resulting degenerate equations admit uniform parabolic estimates that recover control of the physical deformation without a global density lower bound. Combined with compact positivity estimates and a one-sided Glaeser inequality, this closes a homogeneous continuation argument without imposing $L^2$-integrability on the density powers themselves. The solutions conserve mass, preserve far-field vacuum, and remain smooth and strictly positive on every compact spacetime cylinder.

papers.title: Global recovery of a scalar diffusivity from a single final state
papers.abstract: We prove global uniqueness and Lipschitz stability for a scalar diffusivity in the heat equation from a single final state at any prescribed positive time. On each prescribed uniformly elliptic $C^{1,\alpha}$-bounded class with known coefficient boundary values, we choose a constant initial datum and a spatially constant exponential boundary input that work for the entire class. The result holds on smooth bounded connected domains in every dimension $n\ge2$ and gives an affirmative answer to \cite[Problem~8.2]{Alessandrini} within these classes. The stability estimate controls the $L^2$ diffusivity difference by the $H^2$ final-state difference, and this data norm is optimal within the Sobolev scale for the chosen experiment.

papers.title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
papers.abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global H\"{o}lder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally H\"{o}lder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global H\"{o}lder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.

papers.title: Well-posedness for $p(x)$-Laplacian parabolic equations under a multiple-regime setting on an annulus
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an energy-variational framework for the well-posedness of the initial boundary value problem of the parabolic equation with variable exponents on an annulus, under the multiple-regime setting consisting of the subcritical, critical and supercritical regimes of the variable exponents. The multiple-regime setting leads to the appearance of the critical and supercritical regions of positive measure, which cause the failure of the classical Sobolev embedding and the lack of compactness. To address the challenges posed by multiple regimes to well-posedness within the energy framework, we recover the compact Sobolev embedding for a class of radially symmetric functions by the Strauss inequality and obtain the local existence of the solution via the combination of the subdifferential technique and the Principle of Symmetric Criticality for any given radially symmetric initial data. Additionally, the uniqueness result is also given with the recovered Sobolev embedding. Moreover, examining the impact on well-posedness of solutions caused by the variable exponents crossing three sensitive regions, we establish a variational structure of the potential well theory for the evolution equation under the multiple-regime setting on the annulus. For subcritical and critical initial energy levels, we consider the non-positive and positive initial energy cases separately. We obtain the finite-time blow-up of the solution with non-positive initial energy and the threshold condition for global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution with positive initial energy. For supercritical initial energy level, several sufficient criteria for the global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution are given. Finally, the above results, including global existence and finite-time blow-up, are generalized to a more general locally symmetric domain containing an annulus.

papers.title: Linear Stability and a Turning Point Principle for Barotropic Liquid Stars with a Free Boundary in General Relativity
papers.abstract: We study the linear stability of spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat steady states of the Einstein-Euler system describing a liquid star surrounded by vacuum. The equation of state has positive surface density, positive causal sound speed, and an asymptotically linear high-density limit. We construct the equilibrium family and derive the linearized equation with a Robin boundary condition. The linearized operator has discrete real spectrum, and its negative Morse index equals the number of growing modes. We prove that the linearized operator around steady states with large central redshift admits a growing mode, while such growing modes do not exist for steady states with small central redshift. A parameter derivative of the equilibrium family provides a regular interior zero solution of the linearized equation, whose boundary defect is a nonzero multiple of the parameter derivative of the total mass. This gives a turning point principle: the kernel is one-dimensional precisely at mass critical points, and the sign of the crossing eigenvalue is determined by the bending of the mass-radius curve.

papers.title: Coupling perturbations of the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on round spheres
papers.abstract: We study the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on the round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq3$, with coupling coefficient $1+\eps k$, where $k\in C^2(S^m,\R)$ and $\eps$ is small. Morse and degree conditions yield solutions with positive scalar component, and a generic nondegeneracy condition gives multiplicity modulo spinorial symmetries. For a suitable fixed coefficient, we obtain a noncompact solution sequence with infinitely many distinct energy values. A Kazdan-Warner identity gives nonexistence for a smooth Morse potential and its small $C^2$-perturbations, even with positive coupling. The existence proofs use a local reduction in the interior of the positive cone, accommodating the negative powers occurring when $m\geq5$.

papers.title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
papers.abstract: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $\beta=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}\lambda_D^{-\beta/2}(1+O(\lambda_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(\lambda_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(\lambda_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.

papers.title: Well-posedness for the Cubic Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation With Nonlinearity Supported on a Hypersurface
papers.abstract: We prove that the 2-d cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with nonlinearity supported on a line or a sphere is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\). For higher dimensions, we prove that the equation with hyperplane-supported nonlinearity is locally well-posed in suitable anisotropic Sobolev spaces. We also prove that the equation with sphere-supported nonlinearity is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for radial data.

papers.title: Semilinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the semilinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with a harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities. The goal is to classify initial data that lead to either global existence or blowup solutions by using an enhanced cross-constrained variational theory. First, we review and analyze this variational approach, pinpointing the main issue for our specific problem. We then introduce new variational structures by carefully selecting terms in the energy functional and adjusting their weights, enabling us to create eight cross-constrained variational combinations and related manifolds to distinguish initial data that result in global solutions or finite-time blowup. Using these structures, we examine three initial energy levels: negative, non-negative low, and high energy. Notably, we prove that for any initial data with negative energy, solutions blow up in finite time regardless of their size. Throughout the study, we utilize these new variational frameworks and functionals to systematically classify initial data for global existence or finite-time blowup. We highlight the comprehensiveness of our approach as we analyze numerous combinations of the energy and mass terms, despite the complexity involved. Interestingly, we find that when initial energy is minimized, classifications based on different functionals coincide. For high initial energy, an unresolved issue even for the standard Schr\"{o}dinger equation, we develop a strategy controlling bounds of energy to classify the solution dynamics, including global existence or blowup, for our model. We also provide a complete proof for the standard case addressing this open problem.

papers.title: Geometry property of stochastic parabolic equations and Pr\'{e}kopa-Leindler inequality on bounded domains
papers.abstract: We study the preservation of spatial concavity and log-concavity for stochastic parabolic equations posed on bounded convex domains. For the linear noise, by using Minkowski convolutions, we establish the convexity preservation of solution almost surely. For the nonlinear noise, by using It\^{o} formula, the impact of noise is given. Moreover, we establish the relationship between the weighted (stochastic) Pr\'{e}kopa-Leindler inequality and properties of (stochastic) parabolic equation on bounded domain, which is new even for deterministic case.

papers.title: Optimal time decay of the Boltzmann equation with cutoff soft potentials in the whole space
papers.abstract: Since Strain's work \cite{Strain-2012-KRM} on almost optimal time decay rates for the microscopic part of perturbative classical solutions to the Boltzmann system with soft potentials via the time-velocity splitting method, how to obtain the optimal decay of the microscopic part has remained unsolved. In this paper, we resolve this problem by developing a nonlinear energy estimate method different from the time-velocity splitting approach. The proof relies on a combination of a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, the damping factor \(e^{-\nu(v)(t-\tau)}\), and a dyadic decomposition of velocity space.

papers.title: Peaking self-similar solutions and continuation after blow-up for a quasilinear Hardy-H\'enon equation
papers.abstract: We consider the quasilinear Hardy-H\'enon equation $$ u_t=\Delta u^m+|x|^{\sigma}u^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,T), $$ in the range of exponents and dimension $$ N\geq3, \quad \sigma\in(-2,\infty), \quad m>1, \quad p>p_S(\sigma)=\frac{m(N+2\sigma+2)}{N-2}. $$ We establish sharp ranges of exponents $(m,p,\sigma)$ guaranteeing existence of \emph{peaking solutions} in backward self-similar form $$ u(x,t)=(T-t)^{-\alpha}f(|x|(T-t)^{-\beta}). $$ By peaking solutions we understand solutions blowing up at a finite time $T\in(0,\infty)$ but allowing for a continuation after the blow-up time. As a remarkable outcome, a number of ranges of exponents $\sigma$ and $m$ for which peaking solutions exist for any $p>p_S(\sigma)$ are deduced, contrasting to the previously considered exponent $\sigma=0$, where a Lepin-type critical exponent $p_L$ provides an upper bound for $p$.

papers.title: Bilinear Strichartz estimates on the hyperbolic space and the cubic NLS
papers.abstract: We prove bilinear Strichartz estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on the hyperbolic space. These bilinear estimates are then applied, as part of an I-method argument, to establish global well-posedness for the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the hyperbolic plane for regularities above 4/7. The I-method is implemented in physical space using a heat-based modified energy.

papers.title: Energies with values in networks and geometric quasiconvexity
papers.abstract:
We study the asymptotic behaviour, as $\varepsilon	o 0^+$, of the $p$-Dirichlet energy of maps $u\colon\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2 	o \mathbb{R}^2$ constrained to take values in the rescaled periodic network $\varepsilon\mathcal Z$, where $\mathcal Z$ is a standard square network in $\mathbb{R}^2$. The oscillations are carried by the constraint in the target, not by the energy density, and their effect depends on $p$. For $1<p<2$ the constraint disappears in the limit: the $\Gamma$-limit is an integral functional on the whole of $m{W}^{1,p}(\Omega , \mathbb{R}^2 )$, whose density is given by an asymptotic cell formula on tilted cells. This density is equal to $(|a_1|+|a_2|)^p$ on rank-one matrices $a\otimes
u$, $|
u|=1$, and exceeds its convex envelope by a quantity comparable to $|\det A|\,|A|^{p-2}$, with constants of order $(2-p)^{-1}$. Consequently, although the original energy density is convex, the limit density is quasiconvex but neither convex nor polyconvex: quasiconvexity is generated by the geometry of the constraint. For $p\ge2$ the constraint survives in the limit as $\det
abla u=0$, and the $\Gamma$-limit is the degenerate energy $\int_\Omega(|
abla u_1|+|
abla u_2|)^p\, m{d} x$, that is, the $p$-energy of $u$ considered as a map into the normed plane $(\mathbb{R}^2,|\cdot|_1)$, the metric limit of the networks.

papers.title: Uniform Regularity for the Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System under Navier-Slip Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the existence of a local-in-time strong solution to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in a three-dimensional bounded smooth domain, subject to the general Navier--slip boundary condition. The solution is shown to be uniformly bounded in conormal Sobolev spaces, with uniform regularity estimates that are independent of the viscosity coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain the inviscid limit to the corresponding compressible Euler--Poisson system via a strong compactness argument.

papers.title: Characterization of intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type
papers.abstract: We characterize metric measure spaces that satisfy intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type. The considered parabolic Harnack inequalities are intrinsic in the sense that the waiting time depends on the solution. Our main results shows that in a metric measure space with a doubling measure, such an intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequality holds if and only if a Poincar\'e inequality holds. We thus show that estimates in scale and function dependent intrinsic geometries can characterize scale and location invariant functional inequalities.

papers.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).

papers.title: From kinetic activation dynamics to Holling type reaction-diffusion predator-prey systems
papers.abstract: We consider a kinetic model of predator-prey dynamics in which predation is characterized by a sequence of behavioral transitions. Prey and predators are described by distribution functions in phase space, with the predator population further structured into internal states corresponding to inactive, active, and saturated individuals. We show that different macroscopic functional responses emerge from distinct mechanisms governing predator activation. More precisely, activation driven uniquely by pairwise encounters leads to a saturating Holling type II response, whereas activation additionally modulated by local prey density produces a generalized sigmoidal Holling type III response. This is achieved by means of a diffusive scaling and a formal hydrodynamic limit, from which we derive a closed reaction-diffusion system of Rosenzweig-MacArthur type for the prey and total predator spatial densities.

papers.title: The effect of the permeability in interface problems: impermeable barriers and free diffusion
papers.abstract: Focusing on reaction-diffusion models with an interface region dividing the domain, we study the stability of systems as the permeability parameter approaches zero or infinity under Kedem-Katchalsky boundary conditions imposed on the membrane or interface region. These boundary conditions establish that the flux across the interface manifold is proportional to the density jump across that region, with the constant of proportionality defined as the permeability parameter. We analyze both limiting behaviors: when permeability vanishes and when infinite flux is permitted. This analysis is carried out for both the well-known symmetric case, where permeability is identical in both directions across the membrane, and the asymmetric case, where it depends on the direction of the flux. For the asymmetric case, we obtain novel and surprising results that reveal a richer variety of behaviors in this class of interface problems and that differ from the scalar models.

papers.title: Inverse problems and continuity of heat content coefficients
papers.abstract: We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.

papers.title: Sharpness transitions for weighted Triebel--Lizorkin Hardy inequalities with p < q
papers.abstract: For fractional difference energies with two power weights and distinct inner and outer exponents, we determine regimes in which the constant generated by the homogeneous power is optimal and regimes in which it loses optimality. In the range $1<p<q$, we prove sharp Hardy inequalities on nontrivial weight intervals for every sign of $D=d+2\beta-sp$, including a two-sided interval in the balanced case $D=0$. For $q\ge2$, these intervals extend strictly beyond an elementary pointwise scalar criterion. For $1<p<q<2$, we determine the optimal power exponent in the scalar supporting-line inequality and obtain a larger explicit sharpness interval. The proof pairs opposite logarithmic displacements and controls the nonlinear deficit by a quadratic reference energy of the transformed function. Its translation estimate allows a positive contribution at bounded scales to absorb negative contributions at remote scales. Concentrating tests prove strict loss of homogeneous sharpness near both finite-energy endpoints, and angular variations give concrete bounds for the first sharpness threshold. We extend the method to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, retaining the distinction between ambient finite-energy conditions and finiteness of the homogeneous candidate. We also treat the complementary order $p>q$, including flat-subspace inequalities and a complete alternative proof for point singularities. All sharpness sequences belong to the specified smooth test classes, and every positive optimal constant extends to their completion in the difference norm.

papers.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
papers.abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -\Delta u=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

papers.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
papers.abstract: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_\epsilon$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $\epsilon$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.

papers.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
papers.abstract: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $\alpha$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($\alpha = 0)$ and the SQG equation $(\alpha = 1)$. We prove that, for every $\alpha \in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$.

papers.title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
papers.abstract: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.

papers.title: From entropy waves to vortex sheets for the Euler equations
papers.abstract: We construct piecewise smooth solutions of the full compressible Euler equations that evolve from entropy waves into vortex sheets while retaining a strictly positive Taylor jump. For every integer $\kappa\geq1$, we obtain solutions satisfying initial material compatibility for pressure and velocity through order $\kappa$, whose tangential velocity jump has a nonzero leading term of order $t^{\kappa+1}$. These solutions are periodic in the tangential variables and admit a smooth realization in a slab with impermeable walls. We also construct solutions on a local nonperiodic tangential patch that satisfy initial material compatibility at every order, yet have a tangential velocity jump that is nonzero for every sufficiently small positive time and flat at $t=0$. The finite-order construction uses a normal Cauchy-Kowalevski problem for velocity potentials, whereas the all-order construction uses a homogeneous reduction to a smooth hyperbolic Cauchy problem.
